title: terraform: refactor private GPU node pools, IAM and networking state layout
author: Priya Singh
description:
Motivation: Private deployment teams need to support multiple GPU node pools per cluster (burst, inference, batch) and cleaner isolation of IAM and networking state. The current monolithic state layout made incremental upgrades fragile and blocked per-pool lifecycle operations. This PR refactors the Terraform module layout to separate node pools, IAM roles/policies, and VPC/networking into clearer submodules and introduces a state migration plan. Changes are backward-compatible at the resource-level where possible but require an automated state migration for existing installations.

What this PR does:
- Introduces modules/gpu_node_pools/ to model a list of node pools rather than a single pool resource.
- Splits iam/ into roles.tf and policies.tf and scopes role attachment to the pool lifecycle.
- Moves VPC/networking state to networking/vpc.tf and exposes explicit outputs for subnets used by node pools.
- Adds state/backends.tf with consistent naming conventions to support multiple TF workspaces (private-prod, private-stage).
- Adds scripts/terraform/state-migrate.sh to perform terraform state mv + import for existing setups; includes dry-run mode.
- Updates examples/private-deploy/ to show multi-pool configuration and documented migration steps.

Compatibility & migration:
- Existing clusters will need to run the included state-migrate.sh which performs verified terraform state mv operations and validates drift before applying. The script logs operations and can be run with --dry-run. The PR includes an opt-in migration plan in docs/terraform/migrations.md.

Testing & validation:
- Unit: terraform validate across modules.
- Integration: smoke deploys to a staging VPC using the new layout, created two GPU pools and exercised rolling upgrades and node draining.
- E2E: ran private deployment e2e job against a small cluster (g4dn-equivalent) to validate IAM bindings and node pool autoscaling hooks.

Checklist:
- [x] module refactor and tests
- [x] migration script and docs
- [x] examples updated
- [x] reviewers addressed comments
- [x] CI green after reruns

Linked items: Linear ENG-4521 (private nodepool lifecycle), INFRA-903 (state layout), OPS-112 (migration runbook).

Notes: Because this touches state layout there is a small maintenance window recommended when performing the migration (see migrations.md). Rolling deploys were exercised to minimize downtime.

release_notes:
- Refactor Terraform state layout for private deployments to support multiple GPU node pools and clear separation of IAM and networking modules.
- Added state migration tooling (scripts/terraform/state-migrate.sh) and migration docs.
- Examples updated for multi-pool configurations.
migration_instructions: Run scripts/terraform/state-migrate.sh against your existing terraform workspace. Typical sequence: 1) git checkout main and pull this change, 2) ./scripts/terraform/state-migrate.sh --workspace private-prod --dry-run to see proposed state moves, 3) review and run without --dry-run to perform state mv operations, 4) terraform plan to validate, 5) terraform apply. The script supports --backup to record current state file and outputs a trace log in /tmp/tf-migrate-<timestamp>. Refer to docs/terraform/migrations.md for step-by-step guidance and rollback notes.
